5.4.3 Dependency: Examples and Constraints
Note that requiredEntries and expectedCallbacks do also include calls in in-
terrupt context. An example could be as follows:
Consider we want to describe the callback-dependencies of an external EEPROM
driver module from the (standardized) AUTOSAR SPI module. Consider the SPI driver
offers an outgoing callback "EndJobNotiﬁcation" always called in interrupt context. To
describe the dependency we would have to create an instance BswModuleDescrip-
tion.bswModuleDependency and do the following assignments:
• bswModuleDependency.targetModuleId = module identiﬁer of the SPI
driver
• bswModuleDependency.expectedCallback = signature+name of "‘EndJob-
Notiﬁcation"
• bswModuleDependency.expectedCallback.callType = ’callback’

’interrupt’ (i.e. the required context)
